frequency_question: How often do central bank boards activate or raise a discretionary macroprudential capital buffer above its baseline level when given the statutory power to do so over a multi-year window?
membership_rule: Includes independent central banking jurisdictions with explicit countercyclical capital buffer mandates (e.g., Basel III adopters) active between 2010 and the present; excludes jurisdictions without statutory CCyB tools or where buffers are entirely rule-mechanical without principal discretion.
coverage_note: 5 hits out of 7 major jurisdictions observed; the U.S. Federal Reserve remains the primary major holdout maintaining a 0% setting.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging market jurisdictions that implemented CCyBs early; focuses on advanced economies with comparable financial sector depths.
skeleton: 7 major advanced-economy central banking jurisdictions tracked over a 16-year post-crisis window where the tool was available, yielding multiple distinct activation decisions by the principal body.
multiplier: 5 positive activations across distinct major jurisdictions out of 7 major jurisdictions evaluated in the post-crisis era
validity_reason: The regulatory framework of Basel III capital buffers remains stable and institutionalized across central banking governance models for the foreseeable decade.
